title: Microfluidic vessels-on-chip platform using human pluripotent stem cell-derived endothelial cells
author: Remmert, Otgonbayar, et al.
materials: •For a 3% agarose solution, mix 0.3 g of agarose with 10 mL of PBS −/−.•Resuspend the solution and transfer 1 mL into each 2 mL Eppendorf tube.•Place the tubes in a ThermoMixer (Eppendorf) at 95°C and heat until the agarose is completely dissolved and homogeneous.•The agarose will solidify when cooled to RT.•Solidified agarose can be stored in Eppendorf tubes at RT for 2 years.•For use in the cell extraction process, the agarose can be reheated.

This section describes the extraction of single cells from the vessel-on-chip for further analysis. This enables the examination of vascular structures using state-of-the-art technologies such as scRNA-seq or proteomics. Since the seeding process causes cells to grow in the plastic channels of the inlets and outlets, a special extraction technique must be used to isolate only cells from the hydrogel. To achieve this, agarose can be filled into the inlet and outlet chambers to block the connection between the hydrogel chamber and the plastic part. Like this, only the cells from the hydrogel chamber can be extracted.83.Preheat a 3% agarose solution at 95°C and 1000 rpm in a ThermoMixer (Eppendorf).84.Rinse the cells on the chip by adding 70 μL PBS −/− to each inlet, outlet, and hydrogel chamber.85.Aspirate the PBS from the chip chambers and discard it.86.Block the inlet and outlet ports with 20 μL of pre-warmed agarose (95°C).Note: As the agarose solution solidifies within seconds, it needs to be pipetted directly from the ThermoMixer (Eppendorf) into the ports.87.Prepare an Accutase-ColP solution on ice (materials and equipment).a.To dissolve hydrogels in 6 chambers, mix 210 μL of ColP with 210 μL of Accutase.Note: The Accutase-ColP solution is need for the digestion of the collagen type I hydrogel and the generation of a single-cell suspension.88.Add 70 μL of the Accutase-ColP solution on top of each hydrogel.89.Incubate for 30 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 or until the hydrogel is visibly dissolved.CRITICAL: It is important that the hydrogel is completely dissolved and the vascular structures dissociate into single cells. If a single-cell suspension is not achieved after 30 min, prolong the incubation time. Careful pipetting can also help dissociate the cells but avoid high shear stress as it can damage the cells. Prefer prolonged incubation times over mechanical dissociation.90.Collect the cell suspensions in Eppendorf tubes.91.Stop the reaction by adding an equal volume of PBS + 2% BSA.Note: To ensure the collection of all cells, the gel chambers can be washed with PBS + 2% BSA. Check under a microscope for a successful collection of cells. The maximum yield of cells per lumen is approximately 3000 cells. Make sure to collect as much cells as possible to provide sufficient cellular input for downstream analysis. Depending on the downstream analysis, the necessary cell concentration will vary.92.Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min, at RT.93.Discard the supernatant.94.Resuspend in 500–1000 μL PBS + 2% BSA.95.Repeat steps 92–94.96.Count the cells (see step 53).97.Use the cell suspensions for downstream analysis such as scRNA-seq, proteomic analysis, or other functional assays (see Marder and Remmert et al.1).CRITICAL: For scRNA-seq protocols, a cell viability of >80% is strongly recommended.

steps.title: Download and cut adhesive foil
steps.instruction: Download the adhesive‑foil cut file (AdhesiveFoil_CutFile.svg) from the GitHub repository (https://github.com/MeierLabMiBioEng/Protocol-to-generate-stem-cell-derived-vessels-on-chip) or Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12742938).

steps.title: Prepare adhesive foil on substrate
steps.instruction: Adhere the double‑sided adhesive foil to a flat wooden or plastic board using tape on the edges; ensure the substrate is completely flat to avoid irregular cut depth.

steps.title: Set laser cutter parameters
steps.instruction: Set the laser cutter speed to 250 and power to 20 (power 23 cuts all three layers; cutting only two layers – sticky foil and protective film – is recommended for easier handling).

steps.title: Prepare nylon filaments
steps.instruction: Stretch each filament around a straight object (e.g., microtube rack) and heat at 80 °C for 10 min; allow to cool to room temperature (20‑25 °C); place on a cutting board and cut at a 45° angle to a length of ~16 mm; inspect cuts under a microscope for cleanliness.

steps.title: Prepare VEGFA stock solution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lyophilized human VEGFA165 (100 µg) at 13 000 rpm for 30‑60 s at RT; reconstitute in 1 mL sterile ultrapure water to obtain 100 µg/mL; aliquot 20 µL into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, label, store at –20 °C (up to 12 months); once thawed, keep aliquots at 4 °C for 1 week.

steps.title: Prepare FGF2 stock solution
steps.instruction: Reconstitute lyophilized human FGF2 (50 µg) in 500 µL sterile ddH₂O to obtain 100 µg/mL; aliquot 20 µL into 1.5 mL tubes, label, store at –20 °C (minimum 6 months); once thawed, keep at 4 °C for 1 week (vendor provides exact expiration date).

steps.title: Prepare fibronectin stock and coating
steps.instruction: Reconstitute 1 mg lyophilized bovine plasma fibronectin in 1 mL sterile ddH₂O to make a 1 mg/mL stock; aliquot 60 µL, store at –20 °C for up to 12 months. For coating, dilute 60 µL stock into 12 mL PBS‑/‑ to obtain 5 µg/mL; store coating solution at 4 °C for 1 month (PBS‑/‑ can be used at RT).

steps.title: Prepare collagen neutralization solution
steps.instruction: Make 1 N NaOH by dissolving 4.0 g NaOH in 100 mL ddH₂O. For 1 mL of 2.5 mg/mL collagen (stock 4.63 mg/mL): mix 0.54 mL collagen, 0.10 mL 10× PBS, 8 µL (0.008 mL) 1 N NaOH, and 0.352 mL ddH₂O. Titrate with pH strips (5 µL on strip) to pH 7.4 (8 µL NaOH required for this batch). Scale up to 10 mL: 2.174 mL 10× PBS, 7.652 mL ddH₂O, 0.174 mL 1 N NaOH; filter through 0.2 µm filter, store at 4 °C (up to 1 year). For one chip, use 250 µL collagen solution (0.135 mL collagen + 0.115 mL neutralization).

steps.title: Prepare EGM‑2 complete medium
steps.instruction: Combine 495 mL EGM‑2 basal medium, 12.6 mL EGM‑2 SupplementMix, and 5 mL penicillin‑streptomycin (1 %); total volume 506.5 mL. Medium is stable ≥4 weeks at 4 °C; supplement can be aliquoted and stored at –20 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Prepare Accutase‑Collagenase P solution
steps.instruction: Prepare Collagenase P stock (18 U/mL) by dissolving 100 mg Collagenase P (1.7 U/mg) in 9.43 mL PBS‑/‑; filter 0.2 µm, aliquot 500 µL, store at –20 °C (up to 6 months). On the day of use, mix equal volumes of Accutase and Collagenase P stock (e.g., 500 µL each) to obtain 1 mL Accutase‑ColP solution; keep on ice and prepare fresh for each experiment.

steps.title: Prepare 3% agarose solution
steps.instruction: Mix 0.3 g agarose with 10 mL PBS‑/‑, resuspend, transfer 1 mL into each 2 mL Eppendorf tube, heat at 95 °C in a ThermoMixer until fully dissolved and homogeneous, then allow to cool to RT where it solidifies. Store solid agarose at RT for up to 2 years; reheat before use for cell extraction.

steps.title: Prepare FITC‑dextran solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg 40 kDa FITC‑dextran in 10 mL PBS‑/‑; filter through 0.2 µm filter; protect from light and store at 2‑8 °C for up to 3 years.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS mixture
steps.instruction: Mix PDMS base elastomer and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio (by weight) to obtain 0.5 g PDMS per chip; prepare fresh mixture for each chip assembly and use within 3 h (or until too viscous).

steps.title: Configure 3D printer settings
steps.instruction: Set printer for stereolithography (DLP) with at least 27 µm resolution. Use burn‑in exposure 20 s, light intensity 3.93 mW/cm², layer thickness 50 µm, anti‑aliasing enabled. Fill resin vat to 1 cm with biocompatible resin (e.g., GR‑10 transparent) filtered through a 190 µm screen.

steps.title: Load and orient chip STL file
steps.instruction: Download ‘LumenChip_PrintFile.STL’ from GitHub or Zenodo, load into printer software, orient the chip so the numbered side prints as the last layer (vertical orientation) to ensure highest channel resolution and open pillars.

steps.title: Print chip bodies
steps.instruction: Load as many chips as possible onto the build platform, start the print, and after printing verify that all six pillars are formed and a filament can pass through the channel (fine features must be open). Adjust exposure or parameters if needed and re‑print one chip at a time until successful.

steps.title: Trim chip bottom surface
steps.instruction: Using a blade, cut off any protruding features on the bottom side of each printed chip so the surface is flat and smooth (prevents glass cracking).

steps.title: Insert nylon filament through chamber
steps.instruction: With tweezers, insert the prepared nylon filament from one medium reservoir, thread it through the gel chamber, and pull it out the opposite reservoir; always insert from the same side and pull the clean tip through after gel filling.

steps.title: Apply adhesive foil and cut openings
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, stick the adhesive foil onto the bottom side of the chip; cut the red‑marked areas to allow individual sealing of each chamber (cuts may be made before or after sticking). Remove the protective layer to expose the adhesive.

steps.title: Bond glass coverslip to chip
steps.instruction: Press the optical glass coverslip firmly onto the adhesive foil; the adhered regions appear darker. Ensure every gel chamber is completely sealed to prevent PDMS leakage; note the chip is ~0.5 mm wider than the coverslip on all sides.

steps.title: Dispense PDMS into gaps and cure
steps.instruction: Dispense ~500 µL of the prepared PDMS mixture into the gaps between the gel chambers; incubate for 30 min at 80 °C or overnight at RT. Assembled chips can be stored in a dust‑free environment at RT for later use.

steps.title: UV‑sterilize assembled chips
steps.instruction: Place assembled chips (lid open) in a 10 cm petri dish inside a tabletop UV sterilizer (or any UV device) within a biosafety cabinet; irradiate for 30 min at RT; also UV‑sterilize glass coverslips; store sterilized chips at RT in a sterile environment.

steps.title: Perform lumen permeability assay
steps.instruction: In sterile conditions, remove media from both reservoirs; add 50 µL 40 kDa FITC‑dextran solution to one reservoir; place chip on a fluorescence microscope, set a time‑lapse series with 3 min intervals for 20 min (bright‑field and FITC 488 nm channels); start acquisition. After imaging, remove FITC‑dextran, flush each channel with 100 µL PBS‑/‑, add 70 µL fresh medium to each reservoir, and return chips to the shaker/incubator (or stage‑top incubator for longer imaging).

steps.title: Preheat agarose for cell extraction
steps.instruction: Heat 3 % agarose solution at 95 °C while shaking at 1000 rpm in a ThermoMixer until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Rinse chip and block ports with agarose
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL PBS‑/‑ to each inlet, outlet, and hydrogel chamber to rinse; aspirate and discard. Immediately block inlet and outlet ports by pipetting 20 µL of the pre‑warmed (95 °C) agarose into each; agarose solidifies within seconds.

steps.title: Prepare fresh Accutase‑ColP solution
steps.instruction: On ice, mix 210 µL Collagenase P stock (18 U/mL) with 210 µL Accutase to obtain 420 µL Accutase‑ColP solution for the six chambers; keep on ice and use immediately.

steps.title: Digest hydrogel with enzyme solution
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL of the Accutase‑ColP solution onto each hydrogel chamber; incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until the collagen hydrogel is visibly dissolved. If dissolution is incomplete after 30 min, extend incubation (avoid harsh pipetting; prefer longer incubation).

steps.title: Collect and neutralize cell suspension
steps.instruction: Collect the released cell suspensions into Eppendorf tubes; immediately add an equal volume of PBS containing 2 % BSA to stop enzymatic activity. Optionally wash the chambers once more with PBS + 2 % BSA to recover remaining cells.

steps.title: Wash, centrifuge, and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 3 min at RT; discard supernatant; resuspend pellet in 500–1000 µL PBS + 2 % BSA; repeat centrifugation and resuspension once more to clean the cells.

steps.title: Count cells and proceed to analysis
steps.instruction: Count cells (see step 53 in original protocol) and use the suspension for downstream applications such as scRNA‑seq, proteomics, or functional assays; ensure cell viability > 80 % for scRNA‑seq.

steps.title: Rinse and fix tissue for histology
steps.instruction: Add 70 µL PBS‑/‑ to each inlet, outlet, and hydrogel chamber; aspirate and discard. Add 70 µL Roti Histofix (4 % PFA) to each chamber; incubate 30 min at RT; wash by repeating the PBS rinse (steps above).

steps.title: Cut scaffolding and retrieve hydrogel
steps.instruction: Using a No. 11 scalpel under a microscope, cut the rated breakpoints of the chip’s scaffolding structure (cut only at the hydrogel edge). Lift the hydrogel block gently with tweezers; if resistance is felt, recut until the gel releases.

steps.title: Transfer gel to PBS and store
steps.instruction: Place the extracted hydrogel chambers into Eppendorf tubes containing PBS‑/‑; store at 4 °C for further processing (paraffin embedding or cryosectioning according to laboratory protocols).
